title: The effect of solar radiation variations on the climate of the Earth

venue.name: Tellus A Dynamic Meteorology and Oceanography

abstract: It follows from the analysis of observation data that the secular variation of the mean temperature of the Earth can be explained by the variation of short-wave radiation, arriving at the surface of the Earth.In connection with this, the influence of long-term changes of radiation, caused by variations of atmospheric transparency on the thermal regime is being studied.Taking into account the influence of changes of planetary albedo of the Earth under the development of glaciations on the thermal regime, it is found that comparatively small variations of atmospheric transparency could be sufficient for the development of quaternary glaciations.
problem: The lack of a generally accepted theory for Quaternary glaciations stems from existing hypotheses being primarily qualitative and contradictory, failing to provide a quantitative physical mechanism that explains how small radiation variations could trigger such large-scale climate shifts.
method: A semi-empirical heat balance model incorporating ice-albedo feedback is used to demonstrate that small variations in atmospheric transparency, caused by volcanic activity, are sufficient to explain secular temperature changes and the development of major Quaternary glaciations.
task: The task is to explain historical climate changes, including Quaternary glaciations, by quantifying the effects of solar radiation variations caused by changing atmospheric transparency and planetary albedo feedback from ice cover.
innovation: This paper introduces a simple energy-balance climate model that incorporates ice-albedo feedback to demonstrate how small variations in solar radiation, driven by atmospheric transparency changes, could be sufficient to trigger major Quaternary glaciations, highlighting a fundamental instability in the Earth's climate system.

kg_extraction_triplets.target_entity_instance: temperature change of 1.5°C per 1% change in solar radiation
kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: In this case it turns out that the change of solar radiation by 1%, with the average for the Earth value of cloudiness equal to 0.50 and constant albedo equal to 0.33, causes the tem- perature change by 1.5°.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: If with the decrease in radiation by 1% the mean temperature of the Earth drops by 5°, then with the decrease in radiation by 1.5% such a drop reaches 9°.
